name: Synaptic Drift Emitter SDE-4 'Lullaby'
description:
The Synaptic Drift Emitter SDE-4 operates by broadcasting a precisely tuned electromagnetic envelope that interferes with the brain's default mode network — the cluster of regions responsible for maintaining baseline conscious orientation. Rather than inducing unconsciousness directly, it causes a cascading desynchronization of thalamic relay signals, producing a state of dissociative fugue in which targets remain physically mobile but mentally absent, wandering without volition or coherent threat response. The effect is reversible within minutes of exposure ending, leaving no detectable tissue damage.

What makes the SDE-4 distinctive is its selectivity algorithm, developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's neurological warfare division after seven years of contested research. The emitter can be calibrated to exclude individuals wearing certified neural dampeners or TESSERA-standard cortical implants, allowing operators to move through a drifted crowd unaffected. This selective broadcast footprint earned it the nickname 'Lullaby' — it puts everyone else to sleep while leaving the user wide awake.

In practice the weapon has a distinctive soft hum at 14 Hz, just below the threshold of conscious hearing, which experienced targets have learned to associate with sudden dissociation. Veteran soldiers operating in zones where SDE-4s are known to be deployed sometimes describe a Pavlovian dread response to low ambient drone sounds — a psychological legacy that persists long after exposure.
legality: Prohibited — civilian use; Restricted — licensed security contractors
specifications:
effective range: 0–18 meters (cone), 0–9 meters (omnidirectional burst)
effect duration: 40–90 seconds post-exposure
power source: Dual-cell bioelectric capacitor pack
weight: 2.1 kg
recharge cycle: 22 seconds between sustained bursts
collateral suppression radius: 12 meters standard, adjustable to 6 meters with exclusion calibration
implant compatibility: TESSERA Mark IV cortical shielding or equivalent required for operator immunity
form factor: Compact sidearm with rotating aperture collar
tactical_use: Favored by extraction teams who need to neutralize crowds without producing casualties that trigger political consequences. Operators typically lead with a burst mode sweep to disorient a room, then conduct their objective while targets mill aimlessly. Effective in hostage scenarios where distinguishing combatants from civilians is difficult. Requires operators to wear certified neural dampeners, which adds procurement overhead and creates a secondary black market for counterfeit shielding.
cultural_context: The SDE-4 has become a symbol of sanitized corporate violence — the weapon of choice for entities that want deniability. In GLMZ's political underclass, being 'lullabied' is slang for having your autonomy stripped without marks left behind, used broadly to describe bureaucratic manipulation, media sedation, and pharmaceutical compliance programs. Carrying one marks a person as either a well-resourced security professional or someone with deeply unsettling intentions. Street medics have started carrying portable EEG patches to diagnose drift exposure in alley clinics.
known_users: 'Shepherd' — a fixer known for bloodless contract resolutions
Undercover law enforcement in high-density civilian zones
story_hooks: A player character wakes up in an alley with two hours missing from memory and no visible injuries — someone used a Lullaby on them, but the question is what they were doing during those two hours.
A shipment of uncalibrated SDE-4 units with no exclusion filtering has hit the black market — meaning anyone using them will drift themselves alongside their targets.
A ZHENG-DAO whistleblower claims the exclusion algorithm has a backdoor that allows the manufacturer to remotely override it, potentially drifting the operators themselves.
A street preacher in the lower districts claims to be immune to Lullaby effects due to a spiritual practice — and the corporation wants to know if that's biologically true.
related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular sidearm with an organic, almost medical aesthetic — resembling a hybrid between a clinical instrument and a compact firearm. The rotating aperture collar at the muzzle dominates the front profile, with concentric rings of brushed metal that suggest precision engineering. The body tapers smoothly from grip to barrel, giving it an almost skeletal elegance. At first glance, it reads as *controlled, dangerous, and deliberately unfamiliar* — something that doesn't fit traditional weapon categories.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 24 cm | Width: 6.5 cm | Height: 5.2 cm (including aperture collar) | Barrel depth: 8 cm from grip
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light in hand — roughly 2.1 kg distributed along a compact frame — yet dense enough to feel purposeful and grounded. Balanced toward the grip, making it feel almost like a precision tool rather than a bludgeon. Sits comfortably in an open palm despite its angular design.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite chassis with nested brushed titanium aperture rings at the muzzle. Internals visible through translucent polymer panels along the slide reveal bioelectric capacitor cells arranged like neural pathways.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray primary body with subtle iridescence in certain light angles. Brushed titanium aperture collar provides reflective contrast. Translucent polymer sections show interior bioelectric architecture in faint bioluminescent trace patterns (charging state indicator).
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body, titanium silver aperture rings, ghost-white translucent capacitor windows with faint cyan bioluminescent charge indicators. Accent details in black anodized metal.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with subtle ribbing designed to prevent sweating hands from slipping. Slightly tacky, almost surgical in its precision-engineered feel. The rotating aperture collar at the muzzle is knurled titanium — deliberately textured for field recalibration.
distinctive_features: Concentric rotating aperture collar with alignment notches for manual frequency calibration
Translucent polymer side panels revealing bioelectric capacitor cells in hierarchical arrangement
Subtle bioluminescent charge indicator running along the capacitor window (glows cyan when fully charged, fades to red at 10% capacity)
Soft thrumming vibration at idle state (barely perceptible, 14 Hz resonance)
Miniature neural-sync feedback LED cluster above the grip (pulses to indicate operator neural dampener compatibility check)
Recessed safety catch integrated into grip frame — almost invisible unless you know to look
Dual capacitor cell access port on rear grip (maintenance/hot-swap design)
Faint Zheng-Dao Bioelectric serial stamp along right frame, partially obscured by grip overlay
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric logo — a stylized double helix — stamped in matte black on the left slide. Serial number etched in micro-font along the right frame beneath the grip overlay. Certification marks for TESSERA cortical shielding compatibility printed in white on the capacitor window frame.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units range from pristine (freshly issued to corpo security teams) to well-worn (veteran extraction gear). Aperture collar shows micro-scratches from field recalibration. Grip texture gradually becomes more slippery with age. Some units display faint scorch marks around the aperture from extended sustained-burst cycles. Well-maintained examples show minimal wear; black-market or looted units often feature cracked translucent panels or corroded capacitor window edges.
